beatEffects.beforeState: Independent Greek cities possess ships, hoplites and local commands, but no common authority yet joins their unequal forces against Xerxes' invasion.
beatEffects.afterState: Delegates retain their separate governments while accepting Spartan coalition leadership, Eurybiades' naval command and an allied line in which Athenian ships and smaller contingents keep their distinct places.

beatEffects.beforeState: Delegates retain their separate governments while accepting Spartan coalition leadership, Eurybiades' naval command and an allied line in which Athenian ships and smaller contingents keep their distinct places.
beatEffects.afterState: The same coalition survives Salamis, Plataea and Mycale: Athenian naval mass, Spartan land command and smaller allied forces preserve Greek autonomy without merging the governments that supplied them.

beatEffects.beforeState: The old common-defence pattern remains visible but is turned inward: Persian pay sustains Spartan naval adaptation, Aegospotami closes Athens' grain route and the Long Walls fall, while the restored assembly and separate poleis survive the victory.
beatEffects.afterState: The coalition, its fracture and its civic members remain legible through later hegemony: assemblies, councils, public law and federal leagues outlast Spartan and Macedonian command, so Rome meets cities still able to govern and combine.

effects.beforeState: An Anatolian farming household waits at the eastern Aegean with seed, livestock and tools, but no worked route yet joins it to European ground.
effects.afterState: A traced crossing deposits seed sacks, sheep, cattle and tools beside an inhabited riverbank; one worked route now joins the Aegean shore to the Danube corridor.

effects.beforeState: One finite harvest lies on the floor while winter food, spoilage and seed grain for the next sowing compete for the same grain.
effects.afterState: The divided store binds present consumption to reserve, seed and the next agricultural year.

effects.beforeState: A traced crossing deposits seed sacks, sheep, cattle and tools beside an inhabited riverbank; one worked route now joins the Aegean shore to the Danube corridor.
effects.afterState: Set side by side, three records at the Iron Gates reveal incoming farmers and established river communities sharing households, food practices, pottery and routes while farming moves up the Danube.

effects.beforeState: Set side by side, three records at the Iron Gates reveal incoming farmers and established river communities sharing households, food practices, pottery and routes while farming moves up the Danube.
effects.afterState: Posts, hearth and storage bays are assembled on one house plot; after the roof decays, the rebuilt frame, worn threshold and remembered plot remain visible.

effects.beforeState: Posts, hearth and storage bays are assembled on one house plot; after the roof decays, the rebuilt frame, worn threshold and remembered plot remain visible.
effects.afterState: New hearths push fields beyond the first house; cleared loess, herd lanes and daughter settlements remain cut into the ground around the growing community.

effects.beforeState: New hearths push fields beyond the first house; cleared loess, herd lanes and daughter settlements remain cut into the ground around the growing community.
effects.afterState: Cleared fields, herds, longhouses and inherited settlement ground now cross the Danube and loess plains.

effects.beforeState: Herds, tents and stores can move across grassland, but the household has not yet joined wagon, traction and seasonal pasture into a westward system.
effects.afterState: A mobile household road runs from the Pontic-Caspian grasslands into the Danube basin and central Europe.

effects.beforeState: Incoming graves carry new paternal descent and speech, while the scale of replacement remains hidden inside separate regional records.
effects.afterState: Three regional paternal-line records align from surviving local lines to sharp turnover; the replaced lines remain dark while steppe-linked descent persists across the map.

effects.beforeState: Three regional paternal-line records align from surviving local lines to sharp turnover; the replaced lines remain dark while steppe-linked descent persists across the map.
effects.afterState: Related lineages of language and sacred grammar remain embedded across Europe.

effects.beforeState: Copper and tin lie in distant regions, and neither mine can produce the working blade assembled at the centre.
effects.afterState: Mine, pass, ship, store and furnace lock into one lit chain; the finished blade leaves every separated source connected to its route.

effects.beforeState: Mine, pass, ship, store and furnace lock into one lit chain; the finished blade leaves every separated source connected to its route.
effects.afterState: The mine, pass, ship, store and furnace chain now reaches north: Baltic amber moves south while bronze and glass move north, and longhouses, ship routes and Nordic workshops give imported metal local forms.

effects.beforeState: The mine, pass, ship, store and furnace chain now reaches north: Baltic amber moves south while bronze and glass move north, and longhouses, ship routes and Nordic workshops give imported metal local forms.
effects.afterState: The connected bronze system remains visible at both scales: the Uluburun hold joins distant mines, ships, measures and palace stores across the Great Sea, while amber routes and Nordic workshops preserve the metal's distinct northern forms.

effects.beforeState: Palace scribes, inventories and Linear B tablets disappear with the archive, leaving remembered names and deeds without their administrative frame.
effects.afterState: Sung names, weapons and ideals preserve the heroic age after the archive disappears.

effects.beforeState: Judgment still belongs to remembered custom and powerful households; no rule yet stands where the whole civic body can return to it.
effects.afterState: A spoken judgment hardens into an inscription beside the agora; rule, magistrate and appeal remain fixed on public ground after the speaker leaves.

effects.beforeState: A spoken judgment hardens into an inscription beside the agora; rule, magistrate and appeal remain fixed on public ground after the speaker leaves.
effects.afterState: Public law remains beside the agora while demes, ten mixed tribes and the Council of 500 extend repeatable civic authority across city, coast and inland Attica.

effects.beforeState: Public law remains beside the agora while demes, ten mixed tribes and the Council of 500 extend repeatable civic authority across city, coast and inland Attica.
effects.afterState: Demes and mixed tribes remain the citizen body's ground while inscription, rotating office, council, court and assembly make civic authority visible, answerable and repeatable.

effects.beforeState: The same coalition survives Salamis, Plataea and Mycale: Athenian naval mass, Spartan land command and smaller allied forces preserve Greek autonomy without merging the governments that supplied them.
effects.afterState: The old common-defence pattern remains visible but is turned inward: Persian pay sustains Spartan naval adaptation, Aegospotami closes Athens' grain route and the Long Walls fall, while the restored assembly and separate poleis survive the victory.

effects.beforeState: Royal power is gone, but command, judgment and public consent have not yet been placed in offices that citizens can repeatedly summon and restrain.
effects.afterState: Consuls, Senate, assemblies and tribunes occupy separate stations around the Forum; veto and annual office remain visible as restraints on Roman command.

effects.beforeState: Italian allies owe men and supplies through separate settlements, but no measured route yet turns those obligations into one repeatable campaign system.
effects.afterState: Measured roads, colonies and cities turn local obligations into continental movement and supply.

effects.beforeState: Consuls, Senate, assemblies and tribunes occupy separate stations around the Forum; veto and annual office remain visible as restraints on Roman command.
effects.afterState: The republican offices remain, but allied service has become a war aim: the laws of 90–89 BC widen Roman citizenship across Italy while enrolment and effective political integration remain unfinished.

effects.beforeState: The republican offices remain, but allied service has become a war aim: the laws of 90–89 BC widen Roman citizenship across Italy while enrolment and effective political integration remain unfinished.
effects.afterState: Italian citizenship remains while civil-war armies carry command toward named generals; under Augustus, censuses, provincial armies and self-governing cities place a durable imperial frame around expanding Roman status.

effects.beforeState: Italian citizenship remains while civil-war armies carry command toward named generals; under Augustus, censuses, provincial armies and self-governing cities place a durable imperial frame around expanding Roman status.
effects.afterState: A common Roman civic and legal status now spans the provinces through service, manumission, municipal office and imperial grant; Italian and provincial cities retain local office beneath the shared Roman name.

effects.beforeState: Christian congregations move between prohibition and toleration while imperial patronage and the Bosporus foundation remain unjoined.
effects.afterState: Four imperial positions end in legal protection and patronage; the merged building path leaves a basilica, harbour and New Rome foundation marker fixed at the Bosporus.

effects.beforeState: Bishops carry competing formulations through separate churches, and an imperial summons has not yet produced a confession that can be copied across the Roman world.
effects.afterState: Summons, episcopal debate, creed and authenticated copies form one council sequence; the written confession remains in sees after the assembly disperses.

effects.beforeState: Four imperial positions end in legal protection and patronage; the merged building path leaves a basilica, harbour and New Rome foundation marker fixed at the Bosporus.
effects.afterState: Constantinople stands at the Bosporus as the fortified capital of the continuing Roman state.

effects.beforeState: Summons, episcopal debate, creed and authenticated copies form one council sequence; the written confession remains in sees after the assembly disperses.
effects.afterState: Piers and pendentives carry Hagia Sophia's dome above codex, creed and episcopal throne; Justinian's Roman Christian order remains visible in law, office and sacred stone.

effects.beforeState: As western imperial officers withdraw, grain relief, petitions, property disputes and wall repair have no settled local household that can carry them.
effects.afterState: Grain, petition, charter and wall are placed in the bishop's household; episcopal archives, estates and civic obligations remain as local stations in a Christian commonwealth.

effects.beforeState: Prayer, work, food and sleep still depend on one abbot's custom, while property and succession can dissolve with the household around him.
effects.afterState: A copied rule orders time, labour, property and succession beyond the life of any member.

effects.beforeState: Grain, petition, charter and wall are placed in the bishop's household; episcopal archives, estates and civic obligations remain as local stations in a Christian commonwealth.
effects.afterState: A ruled capitulary road now runs from court through scriptorium and messenger to county judgment; copies remain beside a bishop, abbot and count.

effects.beforeState: A ruled capitulary road now runs from court through scriptorium and messenger to county judgment; copies remain beside a bishop, abbot and count.
effects.afterState: Three royal shares replace one Carolingian court, while the same books, episcopal sees and monastic routes remain illuminated across every boundary.

effects.beforeState: Three royal shares replace one Carolingian court, while the same books, episcopal sees and monastic routes remain illuminated across every boundary.
effects.afterState: Books, capitularies, bishops, monasteries and delegated offices connect political centres without one western emperor.

effects.beforeState: Reform depends on local patrons and personal alliances; no complete set of instruments yet lets a papal office reproduce its authority.
effects.afterState: Ordered election, records and corporate office limit possession of ecclesiastical authority.

effects.beforeState: Ring, staff, estate, court and levy lie in one investiture, leaving spiritual office and royal service physically fused around the bishop.
effects.afterState: Opening altar, estate, court and levy leaves four labelled burdens held between pope and crown; ring and staff remain bound to the same appointment while temporal regalia and royal service remain unresolved.

effects.beforeState: Opening altar, estate, court and levy leaves four labelled burdens held between pope and crown; ring and staff remain bound to the same appointment while temporal regalia and royal service remain unresolved.
effects.afterState: Communion is restored at Canossa, but crown, obedience and investiture remain visibly unresolved; the reopened road ends at a doorway still divided.

effects.beforeState: Communion is restored at Canossa, but crown, obedience and investiture remain visibly unresolved; the reopened road ends at a doorway still divided.
effects.afterState: Spiritual and temporal jurisdictions coexist inside Latin Christendom without either absorbing the other.

effects.beforeState: Marriage remains enclosed by lineage strategy, with the couple's spoken assent unable to override the kin group arranging property and alliance.
effects.afterState: Mutual consent makes two speaking persons decisive in marriage beyond the lineage's command.

effects.beforeState: Unrelated entrants can share devotion and work, but no vow, rule, property or succession yet holds them as one enduring house.
effects.afterState: Vow, rule, donated property and election assemble a monastic house whose seal, store and offices remain when its founders leave.

effects.beforeState: Vow, rule, donated property and election assemble a monastic house whose seal, store and offices remain when its founders leave.
effects.afterState: A sworn crowd gains council, treasury, officers and communal seal; the same durable outline now governs a town in its own name.

effects.beforeState: A sworn crowd gains council, treasury, officers and communal seal; the same durable outline now governs a town in its own name.
effects.afterState: A body can own, decide and persist through changing members by rule, office, record and law.

effects.beforeState: Merchants know distant markets, but arrival, payment and judgment still depend on irregular meetings and coin carried in person.
effects.afterState: A repeated fair calendar lights successive roads, safe-conducts and settlement days; obligations can now wait for a known market and court.

effects.beforeState: One merchant's household fortune stands behind ship, cargo and voyage, so a single loss can consume property far beyond the expedition.
effects.afterState: Partners place fixed sums beside ship and cargo; the passive investor's committed stake is bounded from his other property while the travelling partner's capital and duties remain separately exposed.

effects.beforeState: A repeated fair calendar lights successive roads, safe-conducts and settlement days; obligations can now wait for a known market and court.
effects.afterState: Contracts, account money, settlement and ledgers carry obligation farther than coin or owner.

effects.beforeState: Partners place fixed sums beside ship and cargo; the passive investor's committed stake is bounded from his other property while the travelling partner's capital and duties remain separately exposed.
effects.afterState: The voyage partnership's bounded contribution remains beside a second written boundary: a premium transfers a named ship's stated hazards to an underwriter, so invested exposure and insured danger remain distinct, priced obligations in the ledger.

effects.beforeState: Northern fisheries, grain ports and cloth towns work to different seasons, with no single itinerary yet carrying their surpluses through the year.
effects.afterState: A seasonal stockfish route runs from Lofoten through Bergen toward grain and cloth ports; summer cargo leaves a recurring northern circuit on the sea.

effects.beforeState: Merchants share a foreign quay, but storage, judgment, watch and representation remain private burdens without a recognised common voice.
effects.afterState: Opening the Bryggen yard reveals warehouse rows, elected elders, common rules and a seal; the enclave can now remember obligations and answer as one body.

effects.beforeState: Opening the Bryggen yard reveals warehouse rows, elected elders, common rules and a seal; the enclave can now remember obligations and answer as one body.
effects.afterState: Separate city governments delegate consent into common embargo, fleet and treaty while retaining their own seals.

effects.beforeState: A seasonal stockfish route runs from Lofoten through Bergen toward grain and cloth ports; summer cargo leaves a recurring northern circuit on the sea.
effects.afterState: Four Kontore return prices, warnings and disputes through the routes to separate councils; foreign yards and city governments now form a northern commercial field without one throne.

effects.beforeState: The imperial title claims a realm of princes, bishops and cities, but no fixed capital or single administrative chain can make those powers answer together.
effects.afterState: Crown, regalia, host and chancery move along an imperial itinerary; each visited estate remains lit with its own court, seal and right.

effects.beforeState: Crown, regalia, host and chancery move along an imperial itinerary; each visited estate remains lit with its own court, seal and right.
effects.afterState: Accumulated rights, election and estate government preserve distinct powers inside one imperial order.

effects.beforeState: Feud remains a lawful instrument among estates, and an imperial proposal has no force until the distinct benches consent and institutions can execute it.
effects.afterState: Electors, princes and cities approve the peace in separate benches; court and regional circles remain on the map to judge breaches and organise enforcement.

effects.beforeState: Electors, princes and cities approve the peace in separate benches; court and regional circles remain on the map to judge breaches and organise enforcement.
effects.afterState: The 1624 confessional baseline, estate rights, bounded alliances and restored courts remain joined to permanent negotiation at Regensburg; the imperial mosaic survives inside one public peace.
